# Halal Certificate Integrity: Issuance Screening & Post-Cert Surveillance (halal-certificate-integrity)

## Problem & How Truth Is Established Today
Halal status in Indonesia is established two ways. Regular route: a business submits ingredient and process documentation via BPJPH's SIHALAL portal, an accredited LPH (one of 79 nationally, ~1,740 registered auditors — Kemenko PMK, 2024) performs a physical/document audit, the MUI Fatwa Commission rules, and BPJPH issues the certificate. Self-declare route (micro/small, "low-risk" products): a P3H facilitator verifies a written statement — no lab testing, no LPH audit — before the fatwa and certificate issue (BPJPH, 2024–2026). Once issued, there is no systematic re-testing: the certificate is a point-in-time snapshot with no continuous ingredient-sourcing monitoring, and no automated check that a logo on a marketplace listing corresponds to a real, valid, scope-matched certificate.

## Buyer & Who Pays
Two distinct commercial buyer segments, split from the regulator: (1) LPHs — mostly quasi-public (university-affiliated) or private (LPPOM MUI, Sucofindo, Surveyor Indonesia) — who are paid by applicants and bear the cost/time of physical audits; a risk-triage layer that tells them which applications need priority lab work is a direct efficiency purchase. (2) Brand owners (mid/large F&B, cosmetics, pharma manufacturers) who already pay third-party consultants (GO-HALAL, Ira Konsultan, KMR Konsultan, JasaSNI) for supply-chain risk assessment and audit prep, and who have a standing commercial interest in defending their own certificate against drift or counterfeit use. (3) Marketplaces (Tokopedia, Shopee, Lazada, TikTok Shop ID), who face growing policing obligations as unlicensed products become illegal to sell from 17 October 2026. BPJPH/BPOM are not buyers — they are the registry and enforcement operators, not customers.

## Documented Failures (cited)
- **April 2025**: joint BPOM–BPJPH sampling found 9 processed foods with porcine DNA/peptides; 7 held valid halal certificates and were recalled under PP 42/2024 (BPOM press release; Kompas, 22 Apr 2025).
- **2023 "Nabidz" case**: a wine-branded product carried a halal label; BPJPH's investigation found the business actor and the P3H self-declare facilitator had deliberately manipulated the application data, submitting it as grape juice; BPJPH revoked the certificate (ID311100037606120523, effective 15 Aug 2023) and struck the facilitator's registration (BPJPH official statement; VOI; Antara, 2023).
- **Structural exposure**: SEHATI free self-declare quota is 1.35 million certificates for 2026 alone (BPJPH, 2026), against ~1,740 auditors nationally and an LPPOM-cited 300–500% surge in applications approaching the 17 Oct 2026 UMK deadline (LPPOM/halalmui.org, 2025 — vendor claim, unverified).

## Bottom-Up ARR Path
Three stacked segments, self-serve/API where possible: (a) LPHs — ≤79 reachable, ACV comparable to a fraction of existing audit/lab spend (Rp2–5M per product audit, BPJPH cost calculator, 2026); a subscription priced under that could plausibly land ~Rp30–50M/yr ($2–3K) per LPH — ≈$150–230K ceiling alone (inference: no named LPH customer confirmed). (b) Mid/large brand owners doing continuous post-cert monitoring — a few hundred to low-thousands reachable via existing consultant channels, ACV loosely comparable to what brands already pay consultants (Rp2–5M+/cycle) — 300–500 customers × $1–3K/yr ≈ $0.5–1.5M (weak: no named buyer confirmed paying for *continuous* monitoring, only one-time audit prep). (c) Marketplaces — ≤10 reachable, high ACV given post-Oct-2026 compliance exposure (unverified pricing) — plausibly $250–500K on top. Combined path to ≥$1M is plausible but rests on inference for count and conversion, not a named paying customer today.

## Existing Solutions (as of 2026-07)
Government: SIHALAL (issuance + public certificate lookup), BPOM–BPJPH joint ad hoc market sampling (April 2025 raid was manual, not a standing surveillance system). Consultants (manual, not software): GO-HALAL, PT Ira Konsultan, KMR Konsultan, JasaSNI — human-driven supply-chain risk assessment and audit prep. Global: Bare Halal (Ilham Lahreche) — an ingredient-intelligence platform, but positioned globally, no evidence of Indonesia/BPJPH-specific penetration found. No funded Indonesian commercial post-cert surveillance or drift-monitoring product was found; the closest prior finding (Program A halal-certification profile, 2026-07-29) surfaced only academic blockchain-traceability pilots, no commercial player.

## Kill Tests
- **K1 (Data access) — PASS.** LPH pre-screening: the LPH already has statutory access to applicant ingredient/supplier data as part of its mandated audit (SIHALAL submission). Marketplace surveillance: certificate registry and marketplace listings are both public. Brand self-monitoring: brand controls its own supply-chain data.
- **K2 (Oracle bound) — PASS, with scope discipline.** The literal chemical fact (pork DNA present) is a physical truth no software determines — the product must be scoped as *risk-triage* (flagging which applications/products need priority lab retesting, using ingredient category, supplier history, import records) and *record reconciliation* (certificate-number/logo match against the public registry), not as a lab substitute. Framed this way, the contested truth (certificate authenticity, elevated-risk pattern) is inferable from records.
- **K3 (Absorption) — PASS.** The April 2025 raid was a one-off manual joint enforcement action, not a funded standing surveillance program; no roadmap, procurement, or budget for continuous market monitoring was found in this search.
- **K4 (Bootstrap bar) — PASS, weak evidence.** Multi-segment self-serve path plausibly clears $1M, but customer count and conversion rest on inference, not a named paying customer.

## Scores
- Severity 7 — documented certified-pork recall event (Apr 2025) plus structural exposure from millions of untested self-declare certificates.
- Revenue 5 — plausible multi-segment path; ACV has partial Indonesian comparables (audit/consultant fees) but count/conversion untested.
- WTP 7 — brands already pay consultants (an inferior, manual alternative) for adjacent work; cited.
- Data 5 — core registry data is public/commodity; any accumulating risk-model advantage is unproven.
- Absorption 5 — no 12-month roadmap evidence, but BPOM/BPJPH's active enforcement interest is an adjacent state program.
- Competition 7 — only manual consultants and academic pilots found; no funded Indonesian software competitor identified.
- Moat 5 — recurring audit/renewal cycles create integration lock-in potential; cross-customer network effect unproven.
- **Weighted: 5.9**

## Upside Flag
Secondary evidence only: the same ingredient-risk-triage engine could extend to Malaysia (JAKIM) and GCC halal regimes facing similar self-declare/export pressure, and to adjacent regulated-claims categories (organic, non-GMO) using the same supplier-risk-pattern logic. No Indonesian evidence tests this; flagged as expansion logic only.

## What Would Kill This
If BPJPH/BPOM stood up a funded, systematic (not ad hoc) continuous market-surveillance program with budget and headcount — unlike the single April 2025 raid — K3 would flip. If no LPH or brand can be found willing to pay for continuous monitoring beyond one-time consultant engagements within the first outreach round, K4 fails on contact.
